description: Conduct an open source intelligence investigation from requirements definition through source collection, verification, and pattern analysis.

steps.description: Define the intelligence requirements, key questions, target entities, and collection boundaries for the OSINT investigation.

inputs.name: investigation-objective
inputs.desc: The goal of the OSINT investigation

inputs.name: target-entities
inputs.desc: People, organizations, domains, or assets to investigate

inputs.name: legal-boundaries
inputs.desc: Jurisdictional and legal constraints on collection

outputs.name: intelligence-requirements
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of intelligence questions to answer

outputs.name: collection-plan
outputs.desc: Sources to query and collection schedule

process: Translate the investigation objective into specific intelligence questions
Identify the target entities and their known identifiers (names, domains, emails, handles)
Define legal and ethical boundaries for collection
Prioritize the questions by value and feasibility

steps.description: Collect information from public sources including social media, domain records, public filings, and breach databases.

inputs.name: intelligence-requirements
inputs.desc: Questions to answer from previous step

outputs.name: raw-collection
outputs.desc: All collected data organized by source

outputs.name: source-metadata
outputs.desc: Provenance and timestamp for each data point

process: Query domain registration (WHOIS), DNS records, and certificate transparency logs
Search social media profiles, public posts, and archived pages
Check public records, corporate filings, and court documents
Search breach databases and paste sites for credential exposure

steps.description: Verify collected findings by cross-referencing across independent sources and checking for fabrication or misinformation.

outputs.name: verified-findings
outputs.desc: Findings confirmed by multiple independent sources

outputs.name: unverified-leads
outputs.desc: Findings from single sources requiring further investigation

process: Cross-reference each finding against at least two independent sources
Check timestamps for consistency and detect potential fabrication
Flag findings that rely on a single source or unverifiable claims
Classify each finding as verified, partially verified, or unverified

steps.description: Analyze relationships and patterns across verified findings to map connections between entities.

outputs.name: relationship-map
outputs.desc: Graph of connections between entities with supporting evidence

outputs.name: pattern-analysis
outputs.desc: Behavioral and temporal patterns identified in the data

process: Build a graph of entities and their connections (shared infrastructure, communication, financial, organizational)
Identify clusters, central nodes, and bridge entities
Detect temporal patterns (activity windows, behavioral changes)
Highlight anomalies or gaps in the relationship graph

steps.description: Assess the reliability and credibility of each source used in the investigation.

outputs.name: source-reliability-ratings
outputs.desc: Each source rated by reliability (A through F) and information credibility (1 through 6)

outputs.name: confidence-assessment
outputs.desc: Overall confidence level for each key finding

process: Rate each source using the Admiralty/NATO reliability scale (A=reliable through F=unreliable)
Rate the information credibility (1=confirmed through 6=truth cannot be judged)
Compute composite confidence for each finding based on source ratings
Flag any findings that depend entirely on low-reliability sources

steps.description: Produce the OSINT investigation report with findings, evidence, confidence assessments, and recommendations.

outputs.name: osint-report
outputs.desc: Complete OSINT investigation report with executive summary, findings, evidence, and recommendations

outputs.name: indicators-of-interest
outputs.desc: Extracted indicators (domains, IPs, emails, handles) for downstream use

process: Write the executive summary answering each intelligence requirement
Document each finding with supporting evidence and confidence rating
Include the relationship map and pattern analysis as appendices
List indicators of interest for monitoring or further investigation

description: Set up and operate dark web monitoring to detect credential leaks, brand mentions, and threat actor activity targeting the organization.

steps.description: Define the monitoring objectives, keywords, and collection targets for dark web surveillance.

inputs.name: organization-profile
inputs.desc: Brand names, domains, key personnel, and product names to monitor

inputs.name: threat-profile
inputs.desc: Known threat actors, industry-specific risks, and prior incidents

outputs.name: monitoring-requirements
outputs.desc: Keywords, entities, and patterns to watch for

outputs.name: collection-targets
outputs.desc: Forums, marketplaces, paste sites, and channels to monitor

process: Identify all brand names, domain variations, and personnel names to monitor
Define credential leak patterns (email domains, internal systems)
List threat actor groups known to target the industry
Prioritize monitoring targets by likelihood and impact

steps.description: Select and configure the collection sources including forums, marketplaces, paste sites, and Telegram channels.

outputs.name: source-configuration
outputs.desc: Configured collection sources with access credentials and scraping rules

outputs.name: alerting-rules
outputs.desc: Keyword and pattern match rules for automated alerting

process: Evaluate available dark web monitoring platforms and their source coverage
Configure keyword-based alerting rules for each monitoring requirement
Set collection frequency and deduplication rules
Test the configuration against known historical hits

steps.description: Triage and validate incoming dark web alerts to separate genuine threats from noise.

outputs.name: validated-alerts
outputs.desc: Confirmed genuine findings with context and severity

outputs.name: false-positive-log
outputs.desc: Dismissed alerts with reasons for tuning

process: Review each alert for relevance (does it actually reference the organization)
Validate credential leaks by checking format and recency
Assess threat actor credibility by forum reputation and post history
Classify each alert by severity (critical, high, medium, informational)

steps.description: Assess the impact of validated dark web findings to the organization and determine response actions.

outputs.name: impact-assessment
outputs.desc: Business impact and risk rating for each finding

outputs.name: response-actions
outputs.desc: Recommended actions (password resets, takedowns, threat briefings)

process: For credential leaks: determine scope (how many accounts, which systems, how recent)
For threat actor mentions: assess capability and intent
For data exposure: identify the data type and sensitivity level
Recommend specific response actions for each finding

steps.description: Produce the dark web monitoring report with findings, impact assessment, and trend analysis.

outputs.name: monitoring-report
outputs.desc: Dark web monitoring report with executive summary, findings, and response actions

outputs.name: tuning-recommendations
outputs.desc: Suggested changes to alerting rules based on false positive patterns

process: Summarize key findings and their business impact
Document response actions taken and their outcomes
Analyze false positive rates and recommend rule tuning
Identify trends in threat actor activity targeting the organization

description: Design a secure architecture for a new system from requirements gathering through trust model definition, control selection, and threat review.

steps.description: Gather functional and security requirements from stakeholders, compliance mandates, and risk appetite.

inputs.name: system-description
inputs.desc: Functional description of the system being designed

inputs.name: compliance-requirements
inputs.desc: Applicable regulations and standards (PCI, HIPAA, SOC2, etc.)

outputs.name: security-requirements
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of security requirements

outputs.name: data-classification
outputs.desc: Classification of data types the system will handle

process: Interview stakeholders to understand functional requirements and threat concerns
Map compliance mandates to specific technical requirements
Classify data types by sensitivity (public, internal, confidential, restricted)
Prioritize requirements by compliance mandate and risk

steps.description: Define the trust model, security zones, and trust boundaries for the system architecture.

outputs.name: trust-model
outputs.desc: Trust zones, boundaries, and the trust level assigned to each component

outputs.name: data-flow-diagram
outputs.desc: Data flows crossing trust boundaries with sensitivity annotations

process: Identify trust zones (public internet, DMZ, internal network, restricted enclave)
Map each component to its trust zone
Trace data flows across trust boundaries
Document the trust assumptions for each boundary crossing

steps.description: Select security controls for each zone and boundary based on the trust model and requirements.

outputs.name: control-matrix
outputs.desc: Security controls mapped to zones and boundaries (authentication, encryption, monitoring, access control)

outputs.name: control-rationale
outputs.desc: Justification for each control selection

process: For each trust boundary: select authentication and authorization controls
For data in transit: select encryption protocols and key management
For each zone: select monitoring and logging controls
Document why each control was chosen over alternatives

steps.description: Design the network architecture with segmentation, access controls, and monitoring points.

inputs.name: control-matrix
inputs.desc: Controls assigned to each zone and boundary

outputs.name: network-architecture
outputs.desc: Network diagram with VLANs, firewalls, load balancers, and monitoring taps

outputs.name: segmentation-rules
outputs.desc: Firewall rules and ACLs for each boundary

process: Define network segments aligned with trust zones
Place firewalls and access control points at trust boundaries
Design load balancing and high availability within each zone
Place monitoring taps and log collection points

steps.description: Document all security architecture decisions, trade-offs, and residual risks.

outputs.name: architecture-decisions
outputs.desc: Architecture decision records (ADRs) for each security choice

outputs.name: residual-risk-register
outputs.desc: Risks accepted after control implementation

process: Write an ADR for each significant security decision (format: context, decision, consequences)
Document trade-offs between security, usability, cost, and performance
List residual risks with their accepted probability and impact
Note any compensating controls for accepted risks

steps.description: Review the completed architecture against known threats and attack patterns to validate the design.

outputs.name: threat-review-findings
outputs.desc: Weaknesses identified during threat review with recommended fixes

outputs.name: security-architecture-document
outputs.desc: Final security architecture document incorporating review feedback

process: Walk through common attack scenarios (external breach, insider threat, supply chain compromise) against the design
Check for single points of failure in security controls
Verify defense in depth: no single control failure exposes sensitive data
Produce the final architecture document with review findings incorporated

description: Manage TLS and PKI certificate lifecycle from inventory through automated renewal, monitoring, and rotation testing.

steps.description: Inventory all TLS and PKI certificates across the organization with their expiration dates, issuers, and locations.

inputs.name: infrastructure-scope
inputs.desc: Domains, IP ranges, cloud accounts, and internal services to scan

inputs.name: known-certificates
inputs.desc: Any existing certificate inventory or tracking spreadsheet

outputs.name: certificate-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete list of certificates with subject, issuer, expiration, key size, and location

outputs.name: expiration-timeline
outputs.desc: Certificates sorted by expiration date with days remaining

process: Scan all external domains and subdomains for TLS certificates
Query cloud provider APIs for managed certificates (ACM, Cloud SSL, Key Vault)
Scan internal services and load balancers for certificates
Record subject, SAN entries, issuer, expiration, key algorithm, and key size

steps.description: Set up automated certificate renewal using ACME protocol or internal CA integration.

inputs.name: certificate-inventory
inputs.desc: All certificates and their current renewal method

outputs.name: automation-configuration
outputs.desc: ACME client or CA integration configuration for each certificate

outputs.name: manual-renewal-list
outputs.desc: Certificates that cannot be automated with the renewal procedure documented

process: Classify certificates by renewal method (ACME eligible, CA managed, manual)
Configure ACME clients (certbot, acme.sh) for eligible certificates
Set up cloud-native auto-renewal for managed certificates
Document manual renewal procedures for the remainder

steps.description: Configure monitoring and alerting for certificate expiration across all deployment locations.

outputs.name: monitoring-configuration
outputs.desc: Alert rules for 90, 60, 30, 14, and 7 day thresholds

outputs.name: notification-routing
outputs.desc: Who gets alerted at each threshold

process: Set up certificate monitoring probes for all endpoints
Configure alerting thresholds (90 days = info, 30 days = warning, 7 days = critical)
Route alerts to the responsible team based on certificate ownership
Test alerting by temporarily lowering thresholds

steps.description: Define the revocation procedure for compromised or mis-issued certificates.

outputs.name: revocation-procedures
outputs.desc: Step-by-step revocation procedures for each CA and certificate type

outputs.name: emergency-contacts
outputs.desc: CA contacts and escalation paths for emergency revocation

process: Document the revocation process for each CA (public CA, internal CA, cloud managed)
Define the criteria for when revocation is required versus re-issuance
List emergency contacts and response time SLAs for each CA
Create a runbook for certificate compromise response

steps.description: Test certificate rotation without downtime to verify the renewal pipeline works end to end.

outputs.name: rotation-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of rotation tests with downtime measurements

outputs.name: rotation-issues
outputs.desc: Any failures or service interruptions during testing

process: Trigger a renewal cycle for a test certificate
Monitor for service interruption during the rotation
Verify the new certificate is served correctly (chain, SAN, expiration)
Document any issues and their root causes

steps.description: Produce the certificate management plan documenting the CA hierarchy, renewal automation, monitoring, and revocation procedures.

outputs.name: certificate-management-plan
outputs.desc: Complete plan covering inventory, renewal, monitoring, revocation, and rotation

outputs.name: ca-hierarchy-diagram
outputs.desc: Visual diagram of the certificate authority trust chain

process: Document the CA hierarchy and trust relationships
Summarize the renewal automation coverage and manual procedures
Include the monitoring and alerting configuration
Attach the revocation runbooks and rotation test results

description: Build a security budget justification from capability gap analysis through risk quantification, benchmarking, and leadership presentation.

steps.description: Inventory current security capabilities and identify gaps against the target state.

inputs.name: current-security-stack
inputs.desc: Current security tools, staffing, and processes

inputs.name: target-security-framework
inputs.desc: Framework or maturity model to measure against (NIST CSF, CIS, ISO 27001)

outputs.name: capability-gap-list
outputs.desc: Gaps between current state and target, categorized by domain

outputs.name: current-maturity-scores
outputs.desc: Maturity rating for each domain in the target framework

process: Map current tools and processes to framework domains
Score each domain on a maturity scale (initial, managed, defined, measured, optimized)
Identify gaps where the current maturity falls below the target
Categorize gaps as tool, staffing, or process deficiencies

steps.description: Quantify security risk in business terms using expected loss from breaches and incidents.

inputs.name: current-security-stack
inputs.desc: Context on what is in place

outputs.name: risk-quantification
outputs.desc: Annualized loss expectancy for each major risk scenario

outputs.name: breach-cost-estimates
outputs.desc: Expected cost of a breach based on industry data and organization size

process: Identify the top risk scenarios tied to the capability gaps
Estimate annualized rate of occurrence for each scenario
Estimate single loss expectancy using industry benchmarks (Ponemon, Verizon DBIR)
Compute annualized loss expectancy (ALE = SLE x ARO)

steps.description: Map proposed security investments to the risk reduction they achieve.

outputs.name: investment-risk-map
outputs.desc: Each proposed investment linked to the risk it reduces and by how much

outputs.name: cost-estimates
outputs.desc: Estimated cost for each investment (tools, staffing, services)

process: For each gap, identify the investment needed to close it (tool, hire, service, process change)
Estimate the cost of each investment (license, salary, implementation)
Estimate the risk reduction: what fraction of the ALE each investment eliminates
Flag investments that address multiple gaps

steps.description: Benchmark the proposed security budget against industry peers by revenue, employee count, and sector.

outputs.name: benchmark-comparison
outputs.desc: Current and proposed spend compared to industry median, 25th, and 75th percentile

outputs.name: peer-context
outputs.desc: Context on what comparable organizations spend and how they allocate

process: Calculate current security spend as a percentage of IT budget and revenue
Compare against published benchmarks (Gartner, IANS, Hitch Partners)
Note where the organization falls relative to peers (below, at, above median)
Contextualize: higher spend is not always better; tie to risk posture

steps.description: Prioritize proposed investments by return on security investment (ROSI) and implementation feasibility.

outputs.name: prioritized-investments
outputs.desc: Investments ranked by ROSI with recommended sequencing

outputs.name: quick-wins
outputs.desc: Low-cost, high-impact investments to implement first

process: Compute ROSI for each investment: (risk reduction minus cost) divided by cost
Rank by ROSI, adjusting for implementation complexity
Identify quick wins (high ROSI, low complexity, short timeline)
Group into phases: immediate, 6-month, 12-month

steps.description: Prepare the budget justification presentation for leadership with risk framing and investment recommendations.

outputs.name: budget-justification-document
outputs.desc: Written budget justification with executive summary, risk context, recommendations, and appendices

outputs.name: leadership-presentation
outputs.desc: Slide deck for leadership review

process: Write the executive summary: risk posture, key gaps, requested budget, expected outcome
Frame investments in business terms (breach prevention, compliance, revenue protection)
Include the benchmark comparison and ROSI analysis
Present the phased roadmap with quick wins front-loaded

description: Establish an ongoing red and blue team program from charter definition through staffing, scheduling, and effectiveness measurement.

steps.description: Define the red/blue team program charter including objectives, scope, authority, and reporting structure.

inputs.name: organizational-context
inputs.desc: Industry, size, regulatory environment, and current security posture

inputs.name: executive-sponsor
inputs.desc: Executive sponsor and reporting chain for the program

outputs.name: program-charter
outputs.desc: Signed charter defining objectives, scope, authority, and boundaries

outputs.name: success-metrics
outputs.desc: Measurable criteria for program effectiveness

process: Define program objectives (detection improvement, response time reduction, vulnerability discovery)
Set the scope: which systems, networks, and personnel are in bounds
Define the authority: what the red team can and cannot do without additional approval
Establish the reporting structure and escalation path

steps.description: Plan the staffing model for red and blue teams including skills, headcount, and contractor augmentation.

inputs.name: program-charter
inputs.desc: Scope and objectives to staff against

inputs.name: organizational-context
inputs.desc: Budget constraints and existing team capabilities

outputs.name: staffing-plan
outputs.desc: Roles, skill requirements, and sourcing strategy (FTE vs contractor)

outputs.name: training-plan
outputs.desc: Certifications and training needed for the team

process: Define red team roles (operator, developer, infrastructure, social engineering)
Define blue team roles (detection engineer, incident responder, threat hunter)
Determine FTE versus contractor split based on budget and exercise frequency
Identify training and certification requirements (OSCP, GPEN, GCIH)

steps.description: Build the annual exercise calendar with scenario types, frequency, and escalating complexity.

outputs.name: exercise-calendar
outputs.desc: 12-month schedule of exercises with scenario types and target systems

outputs.name: complexity-progression
outputs.desc: How exercise difficulty increases over the year

process: Schedule monthly or quarterly exercises depending on team capacity
Rotate scenario types (network, application, social engineering, physical)
Increase complexity over the year (automated scans to full adversary simulation)
Avoid scheduling during change freezes or critical business periods

steps.description: Define the rules of engagement template used for each exercise.

outputs.name: roe-template
outputs.desc: Rules of engagement template covering scope, constraints, deconfliction, and emergency stop procedures

outputs.name: deconfliction-process
outputs.desc: How to distinguish red team activity from real attacks

process: Define the scope section: in-scope systems, IP ranges, and user accounts
Define constraints: no denial of service, no data destruction, no production impact without approval
Establish deconfliction: how the red team signals its activity to SOC leadership
Define the emergency stop procedure (safe word, phone call, email)

steps.description: Establish the workflow for tracking findings from exercises through remediation and verification.

outputs.name: remediation-workflow
outputs.desc: Process for triaging, assigning, tracking, and verifying remediation of findings

outputs.name: reporting-templates
outputs.desc: Templates for exercise reports, finding tickets, and executive summaries

process: Define finding severity levels and response SLAs
Design the ticketing workflow (red team submits, blue team owner triages, engineering fixes, red team verifies)
Create report templates for technical findings and executive summaries
Set up a tracking dashboard for open findings and remediation progress

steps.description: Measure program effectiveness over time using detection rates, response times, and vulnerability trends.

outputs.name: effectiveness-report
outputs.desc: Quarterly effectiveness report with trend lines for key metrics

outputs.name: program-improvement-actions
outputs.desc: Specific changes to improve the program based on data

process: Compute detection rate: percentage of red team actions detected by blue team
Measure mean time to detect and mean time to respond across exercises
Track vulnerability remediation time and recurrence rate
Compare metrics quarter-over-quarter to show improvement or regression

description: Implement continuous attack surface management from asset discovery through shadow IT identification, risk prioritization, and reduction tracking.

steps.description: Discover all externally reachable assets including domains, IPs, cloud resources, and APIs.

inputs.name: known-domains
inputs.desc: Root domains and known subdomains owned by the organization

inputs.name: cloud-accounts
inputs.desc: AWS, Azure, and GCP account identifiers

outputs.name: discovered-assets
outputs.desc: Complete list of external assets with IP, domain, service, and owner

outputs.name: asset-fingerprints
outputs.desc: Technology stack and version information for each asset

process: Enumerate subdomains via DNS brute force, certificate transparency, and passive DNS
Scan IP ranges for exposed services
Query cloud provider APIs for public-facing resources (S3 buckets, storage accounts, GCS buckets, load balancers)
Fingerprint each asset: web server, framework, TLS version, open ports

steps.description: Identify shadow IT and forgotten assets that are externally reachable but not tracked in official inventories.

outputs.name: shadow-it-list
outputs.desc: Assets not in the official inventory with their risk assessment

outputs.name: orphaned-assets
outputs.desc: Assets with no identifiable owner

process: Compare discovered assets against the official CMDB or asset inventory
Flag assets not present in the inventory as shadow IT candidates
Attempt to identify the owner through WHOIS, DNS admin contacts, and cloud tagging
Mark assets with no identifiable owner as orphaned

steps.description: Monitor for changes in the attack surface: new assets, removed protections, and newly exposed services.

outputs.name: change-alerts
outputs.desc: Alerts for new assets, configuration changes, and removed protections

outputs.name: trend-data
outputs.desc: Attack surface size over time (asset count, open port count, exposed service count)

process: Schedule recurring scans (daily for critical, weekly for standard)
Diff each scan against the previous baseline
Alert on new assets, new open ports, downgraded TLS, and removed WAF protections
Track the total attack surface size over time

steps.description: Prioritize attack surface risks by exploitability, exposure, and business criticality.

outputs.name: prioritized-risks
outputs.desc: Assets ranked by risk (exploitability times exposure times business impact)

outputs.name: remediation-actions
outputs.desc: Specific action for each high-risk asset (patch, decommission, restrict access, transfer to managed infrastructure)

process: Score each asset by exploitability (known CVEs, weak TLS, default credentials)
Factor in exposure (internet-facing, no WAF, no authentication)
Weight by business criticality (customer-facing, data sensitivity, revenue impact)
Assign a remediation action and owner for each high-risk asset

steps.description: Integrate attack surface findings with the existing vulnerability management program.

outputs.name: vuln-management-tickets
outputs.desc: Tickets created in the vulnerability management system for each action

outputs.name: integration-configuration
outputs.desc: Configuration linking ASM tool output to the vulnerability scanner and ticketing system

process: Create tickets for each remediation action in the existing ticketing system
Link ASM findings to vulnerability scanner results for the same assets
Set SLAs based on risk priority (critical: 7 days, high: 30 days, medium: 90 days)
Configure automated ticket creation for future high-risk discoveries

steps.description: Track attack surface reduction over time and produce the management report.

inputs.name: trend-data
inputs.desc: Attack surface size metrics over time

outputs.name: attack-surface-report
outputs.desc: Report showing current posture, trends, and remediation progress

outputs.name: reduction-metrics
outputs.desc: Month-over-month change in asset count, exposed services, and high-risk findings

process: Compute month-over-month changes in total assets, exposed services, and high-risk findings
Track remediation ticket closure rates against SLAs
Highlight new risks introduced since the last report
Produce the executive summary with trend charts

description: Design a security data lake from source identification through ingestion pipeline, storage, query layer, and access control.

steps.description: Identify all log and telemetry sources to ingest into the security data lake.

inputs.name: infrastructure-inventory
inputs.desc: Servers, network devices, cloud accounts, applications, and security tools

inputs.name: detection-requirements
inputs.desc: Use cases the data lake must support (threat hunting, compliance, forensics)

outputs.name: source-catalog
outputs.desc: All log sources with format, volume, and retention requirements

outputs.name: volume-estimates
outputs.desc: Estimated daily ingestion volume in GB per source

process: Catalog all log sources: firewalls, endpoints, cloud trail, application logs, identity providers, email gateways
Document each source's format (syslog, JSON, CEF, CSV, proprietary)
Estimate daily volume for each source
Map each source to the detection use cases it supports

steps.description: Design the ingestion and normalization pipeline to bring all sources into a common schema.

inputs.name: source-catalog
inputs.desc: All log sources and their formats

outputs.name: pipeline-architecture
outputs.desc: Ingestion pipeline design with collectors, parsers, enrichment, and routing

outputs.name: normalization-schema
outputs.desc: Common event schema (OCSF, ECS, or custom) with field mappings for each source

process: Select the ingestion technology (Kafka, Kinesis, Logstash, Fluentd, Cribl)
Design parsers for each source format to extract fields
Define the normalization schema (OCSF or Elastic Common Schema)
Add enrichment steps (GeoIP, threat intel, asset context, user identity)

steps.description: Select the storage platform for the security data lake balancing cost, query performance, and retention.

outputs.name: storage-architecture
outputs.desc: Hot, warm, and cold storage tiers with technology choices

outputs.name: cost-model
outputs.desc: Estimated monthly storage and compute cost

process: Define storage tiers: hot (real-time queries, 30 days), warm (ad hoc, 1 year), cold (compliance, 7 years)
Evaluate technology options per tier (Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, S3/Parquet, BigQuery)
Estimate cost for each tier based on volume and query frequency
Select the technology stack and document the rationale

steps.description: Design the query and analysis layer for threat hunting, alerting, and compliance reporting.

inputs.name: storage-architecture
inputs.desc: Where data lives and how it is structured

outputs.name: query-layer-design
outputs.desc: Query interfaces, scheduled queries, dashboards, and notebook integrations

outputs.name: detection-rule-framework
outputs.desc: How detection rules are written, tested, and deployed against the data lake

process: Design the query interface for analysts (SQL, KQL, SPL, or custom DSL)
Build scheduled query infrastructure for detection rules
Integrate with notebook environments for threat hunting (Jupyter, Observable)
Design dashboards for operational monitoring and compliance reporting

steps.description: Set retention policies by data type to meet compliance, forensic, and cost requirements.

inputs.name: source-catalog
inputs.desc: All data sources and their compliance requirements

outputs.name: retention-policies
outputs.desc: Retention period and tier for each data type

outputs.name: lifecycle-rules
outputs.desc: Automated rules to move data between tiers and delete at end of life

process: Map each data type to its compliance retention requirement (PCI: 1 year, HIPAA: 6 years)
Set retention to the maximum of compliance and forensic needs
Define lifecycle transitions: hot to warm at 30 days, warm to cold at 1 year
Configure automated deletion at end of retention

steps.description: Design access controls and audit logging for the security data lake.

outputs.name: access-control-policy
outputs.desc: Role-based access controls for data lake read, write, and admin operations

outputs.name: data-lake-architecture-document
outputs.desc: Complete architecture document covering all components

process: Define roles: analyst (read), detection engineer (read/write rules), admin (full)
Implement row-level or field-level security for sensitive data (PII, credentials)
Configure audit logging for all queries and data access
Produce the complete architecture document

description: Design an annual series of tabletop exercises from scenario selection through complexity progression and improvement tracking.

steps.description: Select exercise scenarios based on the organization's risk profile, industry threats, and past incidents.

inputs.name: risk-register
inputs.desc: Organization's risk register with likelihood and impact ratings

inputs.name: threat-intelligence
inputs.desc: Current threat landscape for the industry

outputs.name: scenario-shortlist
outputs.desc: Ranked list of scenarios by relevance and training value

outputs.name: scenario-rationale
outputs.desc: Why each scenario was selected and what it tests

process: Review the risk register for top risks that have not been exercised
Check threat intelligence for emerging threats relevant to the industry
Identify gaps in the team's experience based on past incidents
Select 4 to 6 scenarios for the annual series

steps.description: Scale the selected scenarios from basic to advanced complexity across the exercise series.

outputs.name: complexity-schedule
outputs.desc: Scenarios ordered by complexity with difficulty rating

outputs.name: learning-objectives-per-exercise
outputs.desc: Specific skills each exercise builds on the previous one

process: Rate each scenario by complexity (number of decision points, time pressure, ambiguity)
Order from simplest to most complex across the annual calendar
Define learning objectives that build progressively (basic triage, then coordination, then crisis communication)
Ensure later exercises assume skills practiced in earlier ones

steps.description: Design each scenario with injects, decision points, and facilitator notes.

outputs.name: scenario-packages
outputs.desc: Complete scenario for each exercise with situation brief, injects, decision points, and facilitator guide

outputs.name: participant-materials
outputs.desc: Handouts, reference cards, and role assignments for each exercise

process: Write the situation brief (what happened, what is known, what is unknown)
Design 5 to 8 injects per exercise (new information that changes the situation)
Define decision points: what should the team decide and what are the consequences of each option
Write facilitator notes: timing, expected discussion topics, correct and incorrect responses

steps.description: Schedule the exercises across the year, coordinating with participant availability and business calendar.

outputs.name: annual-schedule
outputs.desc: Dates, participants, locations, and logistics for each exercise

outputs.name: participant-invitations
outputs.desc: Invitations with pre-reading and role assignments

process: Identify required participants for each exercise (incident commander, SOC, legal, communications, executives)
Schedule quarterly, avoiding change freezes and major business events
Book rooms or video conferencing and prepare materials
Send invitations with pre-reading at least two weeks in advance

steps.description: Track improvements and action items across exercises to measure program effectiveness.

outputs.name: improvement-tracker
outputs.desc: Action items from each exercise with owner, status, and completion date

outputs.name: capability-trend
outputs.desc: How the team's performance improves across exercises (decision speed, communication quality, procedure adherence)

process: After each exercise: debrief, collect observations, and list action items
Assign each action item an owner and deadline
Track completion before the next exercise
Score each exercise on key dimensions and plot the trend

steps.description: Produce the annual exercise plan document summarizing the series, schedule, and improvement goals.

inputs.name: improvement-tracker
inputs.desc: Prior action items and their status

outputs.name: annual-exercise-plan
outputs.desc: Complete plan document with executive summary, scenario descriptions, schedule, and success criteria

outputs.name: executive-briefing
outputs.desc: One-page summary for leadership approval

process: Write the executive summary: why these scenarios, what we will learn, what it costs
Include each scenario description with its learning objectives
Attach the schedule and participant requirements
Define success criteria for the program year

description: Procure a penetration test from a vendor, from scope definition through RFP, vendor evaluation, and engagement management.

steps.description: Define the scope, objectives, and constraints for the penetration test engagement.

inputs.name: systems-in-scope
inputs.desc: Applications, networks, and environments to be tested

inputs.name: compliance-drivers
inputs.desc: Regulatory or audit requirements driving the test

inputs.name: testing-constraints
inputs.desc: Restrictions on timing, methods, or targets

outputs.name: scope-document
outputs.desc: Detailed scope including systems, test types, and boundaries

outputs.name: test-objectives
outputs.desc: What the test should determine (e.g., can an external attacker reach PCI data)

process: List all in-scope systems with their technology stack and network location
Define the test types needed (external, internal, web app, social engineering, wireless)
Document constraints (production vs staging, testing windows, excluded systems)
Write clear objectives that the test should answer

steps.description: Write the request for proposal with technical requirements, evaluation criteria, and timeline.

outputs.name: rfp-document
outputs.desc: Complete RFP with scope, requirements, timeline, evaluation criteria, and submission instructions

outputs.name: vendor-shortlist
outputs.desc: Initial list of vendors to send the RFP to

process: Include the scope, objectives, and constraints in the RFP
Specify deliverables: executive report, technical findings, retest, and debrief
Define evaluation criteria: methodology, team qualifications, reporting quality, cost, and references
Set the timeline: RFP response deadline, vendor selection, engagement start and end

steps.description: Evaluate vendor proposals against technical and business criteria to select the testing firm.

outputs.name: evaluation-scorecard
outputs.desc: Scored comparison of vendor proposals across all criteria

outputs.name: selected-vendor
outputs.desc: Winning vendor with justification

process: Score each proposal on methodology (OWASP, PTES, OSSTMM alignment)
Evaluate team qualifications (certifications: OSCP, GPEN, CREST; years of experience)
Review sample reports for quality, depth, and actionability
Check references from similar engagements

steps.description: Negotiate the statement of work with the selected vendor covering scope, timeline, liability, and deliverables.

outputs.name: signed-sow
outputs.desc: Executed statement of work with scope, timeline, cost, liability, and deliverables

outputs.name: engagement-schedule
outputs.desc: Day-by-day or week-by-week testing schedule

process: Negotiate scope boundaries and change order procedures
Agree on liability, indemnification, and data handling
Set the testing schedule with daily check-in calls during active testing
Define the deliverables, retest policy, and payment milestones

steps.description: Manage the engagement from kickoff through daily status, findings review, and retest coordination.

outputs.name: engagement-log
outputs.desc: Record of all communications, findings reported during testing, and decisions made

outputs.name: preliminary-findings
outputs.desc: Critical and high findings communicated during testing for early remediation

process: Run the kickoff meeting: introductions, scope confirmation, communication channels, emergency contacts
Hold daily status calls during active testing to receive preliminary findings
Escalate critical findings immediately for early remediation
Coordinate the retest after remediation is complete

steps.description: Close the engagement with final report review, debrief, and vendor performance assessment.

outputs.name: final-pentest-report
outputs.desc: Accepted final report with all findings, evidence, and remediation recommendations

outputs.name: vendor-performance-review
outputs.desc: Assessment of vendor performance for future procurement decisions

process: Review the final report for completeness and accuracy
Conduct the debrief session with the testing team
Score vendor performance against the original evaluation criteria
Archive the report and update the vendor performance database
